title: Career roadmap · Translator
summary: Build strong language proficiency, translation technique, subject knowledge, cultural awareness, and a portfolio that demonstrates accurate human and AI-assisted translation.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Reach strong working proficiency in one foreign language, build translation fundamentals, complete 30–50 portfolio translations, and gain internship/freelance experience.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Choose a domain such as legal, technical, medical, business, literary, localisation, subtitling or audiovisual translation.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Move from general translation into specialist translation, review/editing, localisation, project coordination or language technology.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine advanced language expertise with subject knowledge, terminology management, CAT tools, AI-assisted workflows, quality assurance and client/project management.

blocks.label: Timeline assumption
blocks.text: This roadmap assumes a 4-year BA Honours path from 2026–2030. If your university offers a 3-year BA, compress the final-year portfolio and internship milestones into the third year. The language pair should be selected early; German, French, Japanese, Korean, Chinese and Arabic each require a different learning pathway.

blocks.text: 4-year honours variant

Use the fourth year for a substantial translation dissertation/project, advanced language study, research methodology, internship and a professional portfolio. A strong final project could involve translating a technical manual, business material, literary work, website or audiovisual content and documenting the translation decisions.
Specialisation options

rows.text: CAT tools + terminology + AI-assisted translation + QA

blocks.text: Do not remain dependent only on general-purpose translation. Build expertise in a specialised domain, learn terminology management and translation QA, and become capable of reviewing and improving machine-assisted translations. Senior translators can also move into language project management, localisation, editing, training or independent consultancy.

Language Consultant / Translation Agency Lead / Independent Specialist (15+ years)

blocks.text: Progression depends heavily on language level, specialisation, portfolio quality, industry and client experience.
PhD routes
Possible research directions include:
A PhD is most useful if the goal is research, university teaching, advanced language scholarship or specialised language-technology research.

By this stage, the strongest position is not simply “someone who translates.” Build a defensible combination of advanced language proficiency + specialist domain knowledge + translation QA + terminology management + localisation + AI-assisted translation workflows. Experienced professionals can progress toward senior review, language operations, project management, consultancy, training or their own translation business.
